question: For what value of \(x\) does \[ \begin{aligned} &\log_{\sqrt2}\sqrt{x}+\log_2 x \\ &\quad {}+\log_4\left(x^2\right)+\log_8\left(x^3\right) \\ &\quad {}+\log_{16}\left(x^4\right)=40? \end{aligned} \]
solution:
The base and argument in each logarithm are raised to matching powers, suggesting that all five logarithms have the same value. The term \(\log_2x\) requires \(x>0\), which also makes every other argument positive.

Let \(t=\log_2x\), so \(x=2^t\). For each of
\[
k=\frac12,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4,
\]
the laws of positive-base powers give
\[
(2^k)^t=(2^t)^k=x^k.
\]
Thus, by the definition of a logarithm,
\[
\log_{2^k}(x^k)=t.
\]
These are exactly the five terms in the question, with \(k=\tfrac12\) giving the square-root term. All their bases are greater than \(1\), so they are valid logarithm bases.

The equation therefore becomes \(5t=40\), giving \(t=8\). Consequently,
\[
x=2^8=256,
\]
choice D.
